notes.text: The buggy snippet compiles with warning CS8425 (async iterator with a CancellationToken parameter not decorated with [EnumeratorCancellation]). I assume the sandbox build does not treat warnings as errors; if it does, the buggy code would fail to build (only fixedSource is run, which has no such warning).
Warning code CS8425 is quoted from memory as the diagnostic for a missing [EnumeratorCancellation]; verify the exact number.

Claim: when a token is passed both as the iterator argument and via WithCancellation/GetAsyncEnumerator, the compiler-generated code creates a linked token source combining both. Believed correct per the C# async streams design; verify against the docs.

fixedExpect 'canceled\n2' relies on Task.Delay(10, token) with an already canceled token returning a canceled task synchronously, so await throws TaskCanceledException out of MoveNextAsync before a third item is yielded. Traced by hand, not run.
